done_when: The Forge skill says: when a background round, close or merge ends, run forge next at once and do its first step, with no timer; the generated skill copies match; new repos get it at init and existing repos on upgrade and forge sync

known.title: Preserve recovery steps when background commands stop

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a completed worker's branch conflicts with the default branch during a background close.
`src/forge/close.py:200-212` aborts the merge and directs the coordinator to run `forge work`, but leaves the item in its working state. `src/forge/nextstep.py:1096-1109` then recommends `forge close` again. Following the new instruction repeats the failing close instead of resolving the conflict. Similarly, a worker can warn that it left uncommitted changes (`src/forge/worker.py:437-439`), while `forge next` directs close before those changes are inspected; close reviews `HEAD` (`src/forge/close.py:280-283`). These `forge next` behaviors are evidence not addressed by the coordinator's text-only ruling.
Adds work: surface these recovery steps through `forge next`; F 3 x H 2 = 6; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Preserve recovery steps when background commands stop

stop.reason: Owner decided on 18 Nov 2026 that fixes get two review rounds; this is the second

why: Coordinators check work on a timer or a fixed priority list, so a finished round, close or merge can sit until the next check (measured: the median Forge item waits 24 minutes with nothing running)
